newsitem.title: USA: USX posts improved earnings in all three businesses.
newsitem.headline: USX posts improved earnings in all three businesses.

text.p: USX Corp. Thursday posted improved fourth-quarter earnings for all three of its business segments, beating Wall Street's expectations across the board.
Profits at the company's U.S. Steel unit more than doubled, its Delhi natural gas unit's net income nearly quadrupled, while its Marathon oil unit posted a healthy profit.
The company's oil unit, Marathon Group, posted earnings of $160 million, or 56 cents per share, vs. a loss of $336 million, or $1.28 a share, in the year-earlier quarter

USX Chairman Tom Usher said Marathon Group's results were boosted by strong exploration and production levels and noted that 1996 net income of $160 million was the highest yearly income since the group was formed.
The 1996 quarter included some unusual gains, partially offset by an unfavourable tax adjustment and a loss on debt retirement.
Revenues increased to $4.4 billion from $3.5 billion.
Delhi Group, a natural gas unit, posted earnings of $5.9 million, or 62 cents per share vs. $1.5 million, or 16 cents per share in the 1995 fourth quarter.
Revenues rose to $318.5 billion from $233.1 billion.

Commenting on Delhi's performance, Usher said, "The results reflect growth and efficiency gains that are expected to positively impact Delhi in the future." He said Delhi will focus on acquisitions and pipeline projects this year to further improve earnings.
USX's gas and oil units together account for about 80 percent of the company's business. Steel accounts for the remaining 20 percent.

U.S. Steel, the biggest U.S. steelmaker, had earnings of $125 million, or $1.41 per share, its highest quarterly earnings since its formation in 1991 when USX split its business segments into individual operating units.
U.S. Steel earned $61 million, or 67 cents per share, in the 1995 quarter.
Revenues rose to $1.8 billion from $1.6 billion.

U.S. Steel was bolstered in the quarter by a high level of orders coupled with high operating and cost performance, Usher said. He said steel demand should be strong in the first quarter but shipments may face a normal seasonal decline from fourth quarter levels.
U.S. Steel shipped 3,117,000 tons of steel in the fourth quarter, beating the year-earlier period and marking the highest quarterly shipment level since U.S. Steel's formation.

The units also posted improved earnings for the full year with the exception of U.S. Steel, which was hit in the second quarter with a major unplanned equipment outage that cost in excess of $100 million.
Net income for USX as a whole was $291 million in the fourth quarter vs. a loss of $304 million in the year-earlier period. Net income for the year was $943 million vs. $214 million in 1995.
USX-Marathon stock was up 75 cents at $27.75 in afternoon trading; USX-Delhi was up 25 cents at $16; and USX-U.S. Steel was up 50 cents at $31.75, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
